OCTOBER FIELD LOG — CAT HEAD AREA, LAKE MARION

This is a retrospective of our firsthand October fishing trips, not a claim that the same fish are holding there today. October's fishing gave us a documented starting point for evaluating the seasonal move into November.

OCTOBER 5 — Our trip produced approximately 240 pounds of catfish, including four fish over 50 pounds. Wind was reported around 7 mph from the north-northeast to north-northwest. These are trip totals, not a lakewide catch forecast.

OCTOBER 13 — Fishing near Cat Head, morning surface water temperature was about 75.7°F. Bait was observed in approximately 10–18 feet of water. The recorded catch included a 6-pound channel catfish and an 8-pound blue catfish, followed by a blue reported around 40 pounds later in the trip.

OCTOBER 21 — Near Cat Head, water temperature ranged from approximately 70.3°F to 72.8°F during the trip. We caught blue catfish weighing approximately 30 and 25 pounds in about 18 feet of water, and later a blue around 40 pounds in approximately 22 feet on an upslope.

WHAT THE LOG TELLS US — During the documented October outings, productive water included bait-related structure and depth changes in the upper-teen to low-20-foot range. The October 21 upslope catch shows why the relationship between contours can matter as much as any single depth. These results document where and how we fished on those dates; they do not establish a current bite at Cat Head or across Lake Marion.

NEXT STEP — November coverage will investigate a new location and compare its contours, bait, water conditions, sonar observations and actual fishing results against this October baseline. Public reports explain the general-area structure and reasoning; exact GPS positions and advanced tactics are available to Master Fisherman Patreon supporters.

DIVERSION CANAL FLOW ASSESSMENT — November 7, 2026 (11:14 a.m. EST audit)

STATUS: Direct, time-stamped Diversion Canal discharge/current observations NOT independently verified. The Santee Cooper operator feed was updated November 7 and its most recent DAILY lake elevation figures are dated November 6; no synchronized November 7 lake readings or measured canal velocity are supplied. No defensible canal-current strength classification is available.

OPERATOR-PUBLISHED DAILY LAKE ELEVATIONS (date of reading; individual measurement times unspecified): November 6: Lake Marion 74.26 ft, Lake Moultrie 74.17 ft, nominal difference 0.09 ft (Marion higher). November 5: Marion 74.24 ft, Moultrie 74.13 ft, nominal difference 0.11 ft. November 4: Marion 74.23 ft, Moultrie 74.12 ft, nominal difference 0.11 ft. From November 5 to 6 Marion rose 0.02 ft and Moultrie rose 0.04 ft; nominal difference narrowed 0.02 ft. The operator's lake elevations are not individually time-stamped; USGS station vertical datum and simultaneous gauge comparison could not be independently reconciled during this audit. These differences are provisional, not verified hydraulic heads or a flow calculation.

OPERATOR HYDRO SCHEDULE (feed updated November 7; tentative, subject to change): Saturday November 7 Jefferies Hydro midnight–4 p.m.; St. Stephen Hydro not scheduled to run. Sunday November 8 Jefferies 4 p.m.–midnight; St. Stephen not scheduled to run. The November 6 operator facility discharge table lists Jefferies Hydro 4,192 and St. Stephen Hydro 0, versus November 5 Jefferies 4,512 and St. Stephen 17. These are facility discharge entries, NOT measured Diversion Canal discharge, and the page does not identify the table entries as direct canal flow. Scheduled generation is not proof of actual generation or canal flow.

INTERPRETATION — INFERENCE, NOT MEASUREMENT: If the operator's reported lake elevations use comparable reference datums and reflect the same general period, a higher Marion level is consistent with potential movement toward Moultrie. The narrowing nominal difference may indicate reduced hydraulic driving head, but does not establish a decrease in actual canal current. Direction, velocity, strength, navigability and fishing-current conditions remain unverified. Jefferies generation does not demonstrate canal discharge; a St. Stephen 'not scheduled' designation does not establish zero canal flow.

Replaces November 6 commentary.
level_analysis: Daily lake-level readings above are published with USGS station timestamps. Review each gauge's vertical datum before comparing Lake Marion and Lake Moultrie. Water movement and reservoir operations require separate verification; elevation alone cannot establish canal discharge.
wind_analysis: The hourly wind forecast above provides broad guidance, but wind exposure varies by fetch, shoreline orientation, gusts and travel route. Check the selected forecast area, recheck conditions before launching, and do not treat a forecast as a measured on-water reading.
